label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
Sizwe, leave that key OUT, my boy. No more cranking, not even one last “maybe”. Take a breath. You’ve got a wedding tomorrow, not a confirmed R40 000 bill tonight.

Kobus means well, but that’s old Land Rover advice. Your common-rail D-Max can’t take that chance. Don’t put diesel on top: it won’t remove the petrol or make this safe to drive.

Diesel lubricates the high-pressure pump. Petrol doesn’t give it the lubrication it needs, and every crank turns that pump again. Because yours knocked, stalled and then got cranked repeatedly, pump and injector damage is possible. If the pump’s shed metal, that can spread through the fuel system and get expensive. But nobody can tell you from a forum that the engine’s finished, or put a definite price on it tonight.

Tonight’s job: get yourself somewhere safe and arrange a tow, NOT a drive. Check your insurance roadside assistance before paying a tow guy cash; towing may already be covered.

My shop’s in Umbilo, open Saturday 7–12. Thabo, my guy, can get onto it first thing. We need to check the pump and injectors for damage, not just drain it and hope. **If they’re okay**, draining the tank, flushing the lines, fitting a new fuel filter and bleeding it usually comes to **R2 500–R4 500**. That’s conditional, not a promise of the final bill.

For perspective: first year as an apprentice, 1995, I put diesel in the boss’s Golf. He still tells that story at every braai. Apparently the warranty on my embarrassment never expires.

Borrow a bakkie for tomorrow’s cake and sound system anyway. Don’t plan your wedding around a drained tank and crossed fingers.

Congrats, bru. Tonight you organise the tow and the borrowed bakkie. That key stays in your pocket.
